name: global-wind-atlas-era5-expanded
title: GWA 4.0 100 m wind speed, expanded to full global coverage with the ERA5 long-run average
description: The Global Wind Atlas 100 m mean wind speed raster at its native 250 m resolution, extended to complete global coverage using the ERA5 2008-2017 long-run average 100 m wind speed. GWA covers land and near-shore only; this derivative keeps GWA's resolution where GWA has data and interpolates from the coarse ERA5 climatology everywhere else, so that a workflow can sample any point on Earth from one raster instead of branching on coverage. 67 GB, one file.

ethos:upstream.note: Not an upstream product at all: this raster was produced inside ICE-2 by blending GWA 4.0 with an ERA5 long-run average. It exists nowhere else, and the code that made it has not been recovered (see TODO-datasets.md). Its GWA input is separately catalogued as global-wind-atlas-v4. Checked 2026-09-07.

ethos:derivation:
ESTABLISHED: the raster is the GWA 4.0 100 m mean wind speed (GWA_4.0/wind_speed_cog_100m.tif) on its native 250 m grid, extended to complete global coverage using the ERA5 2008-2017 long-run average 100 m wind speed (/shared_data/2026_reskit_long_run_avg/output/global/ERA5_100m_wind_speed.processed_2008_2017_mean_global.tiff, itself produced by that folder's three-step pipeline from RESKit-processed ERA5 and pole-expanded by reskit.util.create_LRA). GWA values are kept where GWA has coverage; ERA5 supplies everything else. Both inputs are named in the filename and both are listed under sources.
NOT ESTABLISHED, and required before this can be called reproducible: how the two were combined at the coverage boundary -- the resampling from ERA5's coarse grid to 250 m, whether there is feathering or a hard edge, and how the seam was treated. No script that produces this file exists in /shared_data/2026_reskit_long_run_avg or in the RESKit tree. reskit.util.create_LRA.expand_to_global_coverage is NOT it: it only fills polar rows and explicitly refuses anything but latitudinal expansion. Ask c-winkler.
